name: ashish-claude-skills
description: Ashish's Claude Code skills: engineering quality gates for TypeScript, tests and audits.

plugins.name: quality-gates
plugins.description: TypeScript types, Vitest and Playwright tests, security, login and access, personal data and privacy, threat modelling before launch, design and UX audits, and CLAUDE.md sync, routed by a hook to the file being edited.

plugins.name: confluence-diagrams
plugins.description: Turns a Confluence page into validated, explorable HTML diagrams through archify, citing the page section behind every node.

plugins.name: plugin-audit
plugins.description: Read-only audit of installed plugins and skills: security scan of hooks, scripts, MCP configs and SKILL.md text, plus a workflow map of overlaps, keep-or-drop picks and hook conflicts.

plugins.name: switchboard
plugins.description: Suggests the cheapest Claude model and effort level that fits each prompt, from a UserPromptSubmit hook that stays quiet when the current model already fits.

plugins.name: feature-flow
plugins.description: New-feature requests run as Opus plan -> checklist -> Sonnet (medium effort) build and test in fresh-context subagents, with a Stop hook that keeps README.md updated.

plugins.name: vibe-coder
plugins.description: Tailscale links instead of localhost for anything running on this machine, and context-saving rules for every coding task, and an improve retro that learns from past sessions' mistakes, and launch-ready / launch-safe pre-launch checks for the pages and the backend. Plus a hook that trims noisy install, build and test output.

plugins.name: pr-review
plugins.description: A one-screen brief for the human reviewer, a splitter that cuts a large diff into small stacked PRs, and agent token spend broken down by PR.

plugins.name: repo-health
plugins.description: Any-stack repo checks: an environment doctor, API drift between server routes and client calls, and vendor-neutral feature-flag cleanup.

plugins.name: design-gate
plugins.description: Checks a built UI against its design mock (Figma, image, HTML or claude.ai artifact) for missing features, content, states and visual differences, gates changes for AI design slop with the mock as the allow-list, and has Sonnet subagents close each gap with a browser check.
